subject: general
question: A spam is a/an:
solution:
The correct answer is __**unsolicited e-mail**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unsolicited e-mail**, commonly known as spam, refers to unwanted or irrelevant messages sent over the internet, typically to a large number of users, for the purposes of advertising, phishing, spreading malware, etc.
 
• Spam e-mails can clutter inboxes, consume bandwidth, and sometimes carry malicious attachments or links that can compromise the security of the recipient's device or personal information.
 
• Most e-mail services offer spam filters that automatically detect and redirect such unsolicited e-mails to a separate spam or junk folder to minimize their impact on users.
 
• Effective management and awareness of spam can help users protect themselves from potential threats and maintain a clean and organized e-mail inbox.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spam** is often sent in bulk by botnets, which are networks of infected computers controlled by cybercriminals.
 
• Users can report spam messages to their e-mail service providers to help improve spam detection algorithms.
 
• Legislation like the CAN-SPAM Act in the United States sets rules for commercial e-mail and gives recipients the right to stop unwanted e-mails, though enforcement can be challenging.
 
• Best practices to avoid spam include not sharing your e-mail address publicly, being cautious of where you sign up for services, and using strong, unique passwords for online accounts.
